The feet were left to demarcate and became mummified (Figure 2), then bilateral below knee amputations were performed.

panels.rationale: Axial contrast-enhanced fat-suppressed T1-weighted MRI of the right foot from a severe frostbite case report, showing nonenhancing low-signal necrosis of the first to third toes (yellow arrows) consistent with gangrenous/mummified necrotic digits, plus bone marrow inflammation and edema around the calcaneal tuberosity (red arrows). Directly demonstrates specific manifestations of frostbite, not a diagram or other disease. [raw subtype: deep frostbite with established bone and soft-tissue necrosis]

panels.figure_caption: Contrast-enhanced fat-suppressed T1-weighted axial magnetic resonance image of the right foot. The first to third toes show nonenhancing low signal intensity compatible with established bone and soft-tissue necrosis (yellow arrows). The plantar soft tissue and marrow around the calcaneal tuberosity demonstrate bone marrow inflammation and edema (red arrows).
in_text_mentions: intraosseous gas on CT. Cold-injury-related bone marrow inflammation was noted in the calcaneal tuberosity, first, fourth, and fifth distal metatarsals, second to fifth proximal phalanges, and fourth and fifth middle and distal phalanges of the right foot, as well as subcortical bone marrow of the medial and lateral malleoli. On the right heel, focal skin necrosis with surrounding soft-tissue edema was observed, but there was no radiologic evidence of involvement of the calcaneus, plantar fascia, or Achilles tendon. An insufficiency fracture of the posterior calcaneus was also noted (Fig. 2).

The photograph was taken in the early days after intensive care unit admission.
in_text_mentions: 70% by plastic surgery assessment. Broad-spectrum empiric antibiotics (doxycycline, levofloxacin, meropenem) were initiated at admission. Blood cultures became positive within seven hours, isolating Aeromonas hydrophila and Pseudomonas species, confirming fulminant Gram-negative bacteremia. Surgical debridement was initially deferred due to hemodynamic instability and coagulopathy. During the ICU stay, cerebral edema improved on serial imaging, and clinical stabilization allowed transfer after six days to a specialized burn unit for the management of extensive cutaneous lesions (Figures 2-3).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Clinical photograph of a human patient's right heel showing a well-demarcated dry black eschar, a classic manifestation of severe frostbite. Disease attribution is supported by the caption ('severe bilateral foot frostbite'), the in-text mention of deep frostbite involving both heels, and the frostbite-focused article title. B: Clinical photograph of the dorsal right foot showing dry gangrenous (black, mummified) toes with desquamation, a textbook frostbite manifestation. Attribution is confirmed by the caption and in-text description of deep frostbite of the right first, second, and third toes. C: Clinical photograph of the left heel showing a large granulating defect, the healing-stage wound following deep frostbite injury. The in-text mention confirms deep frostbite involving both heels, and the panel is part of the preoperative frostbite figure; the drawn line on the leg is a surgical flap marking, not an exclusion criterion. D:...

panels.figure_caption: Preoperative findings in a patient with severe bilateral foot frostbite. (A) Posterior view of the right foot demonstrating a large, well-demarcated, dry black eschar involving almost the entire weight-bearing heel. (B) Dorsal view of the right foot showing dry gangrenous changes of the first to third toes with surrounding soft-tissue swelling and skin desquamation. (C) Posterior view of the left heel revealing a large posterior heel defect with healthy granulation tissue. (D) Lateral view of the left foot demonstrating dry necrosis of the first toe.

His behavior gradually improved with psychiatric treatment, and the restraints were discontinued before surgery. No further as-needed lorazepam or haloperidol was administered from several days before the first operation onward; regular psychiatric medications were continued throughout the surgical treatment period. Examination of the affected extremities revealed deep frostbite injuries involving both heels, the left great toe, and the right first, second, and third toes (Fig. 1).

source_variants.figure_caption: Preoperative findings in a patient with severe bilateral foot frostbite. (A) Posterior view of the right foot demonstrating a large, well-demarcated, dry black eschar involving almost the entire weight-bearing heel. (B) Dorsal view of the right foot showing dry gangrenous changes of the first to third toes with surrounding soft-tissue swelling and skin desquamation. (C) Posterior view of the left heel revealing a large posterior heel defect with healthy granulation tissue. (D) Lateral view of the left foot demonstrating dry necrosis of the first toe.

in_text_mentions: On physical examination, her heart rate was 130 beats/min, blood pressure was 107/55 mmHg, respiratory rate was 20 breaths/min, and oxygen saturation was 98% on room air. The patient was alert and oriented to time, place, and person. Cyanosis was noted in the feet from the toes to the ankles, as well as in both hands from distal phalanges to the wrist. Necrotic lesions in the phalanges and part of the left metacarpals were noted (Figure 1a,b).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Clinical photograph of a 19-year-old male's foot during admission in a case report titled 'Feet Salvage Using Anterolateral Thigh Flaps after Severe Frostbite Injury'. The image shows black mummified/gangrenous toes with associated hemorrhagic/raw areas, a classic severe frostbite presentation. Visible non-necrotic skin on the lower leg appears dark. No explicit ethnicity is stated (only country of origin 'Gambia'). B: Second clinical photograph of the patient's other foot during admission in the same severe frostbite case report. Shows black mummified/gangrenous toes with hemorrhagic/raw areas, consistent with classic severe frostbite. Visible non-necrotic skin appears dark. No explicit ethnicity stated.
